- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent spikes, but true prices often continue trending upward.
- Model lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in upward trends.
- When true prices spike sharply, model forecasts overshoot the peak and then fall too quickly, failing to capture sustained momentum.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 10 days, leading to overly conservative forecasts.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, even when historical data suggests upward momentum.
